# Algae

<!-- BEGIN: hmi-opening -->
<div class="hmi-quick-read">
  <div class="hmi-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>
  <p>Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic and total mercury in algae are reported as monitoring results, studies, references by form and basis, limits, testing and controls.</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Metals of concern:</strong> the metals named by the studies cited on this page.</li>
    <li><strong>Main drivers:</strong> form, origin and preparation stay separate.</li>
    <li><strong>Practical framing:</strong> this page does not pool those studies into one typical value.</li>
  </ul>
</div>

This page draws on evidence from [[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|WHO]] and [[sources/efsa2023-heavy-metals-seaweed|EFSA]], together with 6 peer-reviewed studies. The complete citation list is at the bottom of the page.
<!-- END: hmi-opening -->

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="algae-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="algae-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="algae-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Algae in the HMI library has 221 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, chromium, aluminium, arsenosugar (glycerol sugar), arsenosugar (phosphate sugar), arsenosugar (sulfate sugar), arsenosugar (sulfonate sugar), As(III), As(V), AsB, I, TETRA, TMAO and water-extractable As from 14 For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the algae came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-algae" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-algae-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of algae, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:algae-8a2c9cb95185:adad3edc2ee4"><summary>HMI algae Pb reference · Algae, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:algae-8a2c9cb95185:adad3edc2ee4"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI algae Pb reference · Algae, as sold. Algae, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>1 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>1</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for algae, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for algae, as sold on this basis in the completed algae ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:algae-8a2c9cb95185:adad3edc2ee4</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:algae-e331d2b7d11b:98bb7b45c401"><summary>HMI algae Pb reference · Algae, as sold, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:algae-e331d2b7d11b:98bb7b45c401"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI algae Pb reference · Algae, as sold, dry weight. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, chromium, aluminium, arsenosugar (glycerol sugar), <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-algae-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-algae-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of algae have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of algae have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For total arsenic, the HMI reference median was lowest for algae, as sold (9,050 µg/kg) and highest for algae, as sold (32,200 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-arsenic-contam-2009|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-arsenic-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion on Arsenic in Food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2009;7(10):1351</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-arsenic-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
